title: Proof for education credits (American Opportunity Credit)
use_when: Pick this when the client is claiming or must back up an education credit for a student.
note: Built from IRS Form 886-H-AOC (Rev. 5-2017), which the IRS sends in American Opportunity Credit audits, and the IRS education credits page. Collect these for each student; the form says insurance, medical expenses, room and board and similar personal expenses do not count.

f886-h-aoc.name: IRS, Form 886-H-AOC, Supporting Documents to Prove American Opportunity Credit (Rev. 5-2017)

edu-credits.name: IRS, Education credits: AOTC and LLC (web page, last reviewed or updated 12-Aug-2026)

situations.no-1098-t: A school did not provide Form 1098-T
situations.books-supplies: Paid course-related fees, books or supplies beyond tuition
situations.assistance: Student received employer, veteran's or other tax-free education assistance, or used education savings

items.label: Form 1098-T, Tuition Statement, from each school the student attended
Transcripts or other enrollment forms that verify enrollment
items.detail: Must include the institution's name, federal identification number, dates of enrollment and the student's enrollment status (more than half time, not a graduate student).

items.label: Record of asking the school for the missing Form 1098-T
The school's employer identification number (EIN)
items.detail: The IRS says it must be provided on Form 8863 for the American Opportunity Credit.

items.label: Proof of payment of tuition and fees
items.detail: Canceled checks, bank statements, credit card statements or receipts. Form 1098-T may serve as proof if payments received are recorded in Box 1.

items.label: Proof of payment for course-related fees, books and supplies
items.detail: Canceled checks, bank statements, credit card statements or receipts.

items.label: Documents showing the expenses were needed for a course of study
items.detail: Such as course guides, course syllabuses, or letters from the school.

items.label: Documents showing employer provided educational assistance benefits received
Documents showing withdrawals from any educational retirement arrangements
Documents showing U.S. Savings bond interest that is nontaxable because it paid qualified higher education expenses
Documents showing veteran's educational assistance benefits received
Documents showing any other nontaxable payment received for education expenses
